long_biography.plain_text:
A search for equity participation led Bruce S. Sherman from employment at the Collier family office to co-founding Private Capital Management in 1986. The firm began with one client and grew into a large independent value-oriented asset manager. Sherman sold PCM to Legg Mason in 2001 but continued directing its portfolio management and research before retiring from the business.

PCM's tens of billions of dollars under management represented client capital, not Sherman's personal fortune. His wealth instead came from his ownership and sale of the management company, compensation for investing client money, and investments made for his own account. He later became chairman and chief executive of M4 Capital. Sherman now serves as chairman, principal owner and control person of the Miami Marlins. Professional sport is therefore his clearest current operating business, while investment management remains the foundation of his fortune.
